# [Feature]: Configurable separator between branch prefix and worktree name (#36652)

### Problem or use case

The branch prefix is always joined with a slash: `computeBranchName` in `src/main/ipc/worktree-branch-name.ts` returns `${prefix}/${sanitizedName}`. Teams whose convention uses a dash (`jd-feat-login-form` rather than `jd/feat-login-form`) cannot use the prefix setting, and have to edit the branch field by hand on every new workspace or pass `--branch` from the CLI.

### Proposed solution

Add a `branchPrefixSeparator` setting next to the custom prefix in Settings > Git, defaulting to `/` so existing setups are unchanged. With prefix `jd` and separator `-`, typing `feat: login form` produces the branch `jd-feat-login-form`.

The separator would go through the same check as the prefix (`getBranchPrefixIssue`), and `getConfiguredBranchPrefix` callers that strip an existing prefix to avoid double-prefixing would need to use it too.

### Alternatives or additional context

Including the separator in the custom prefix itself (`jd-`) would avoid a new setting, but `normalizeBranchPrefix` only trims slashes, and the join would still add one: `jd-/feat-login-form`.

Related: #18103 (per-project prefix), #5082 (folder template, whose branch token would inherit the separator)

4	
5	## What changes for users
6	
7	Settings > Git > Branch Prefix now has a small separator field next to the prefix input. It defaults to `/`, so existing setups produce the same branch names as before. With prefix `jd` and separator `-`, typing `feat: login form` creates the branch `jd-feat-login-form`. The preview under the field ("Branches will be named jd-feature") uses the separator. A separator Git cannot store, such as `..`, `//` or `~`, shows an error there. Creating a worktree with such a separator fails with a message pointing at Settings > Git.
8	
9	An empty or whitespace-only separator falls back to `/`. Settings saved before this change have no separator and keep the slash join.
10	
11	## How
12	
13	- `src/shared/branch-prefix.ts` gains `branchPrefixSeparator` on `BranchPrefixSettings` and `normalizeBranchPrefixSeparator`, which maps a missing or blank value to `/`. It also gains `getBranchPrefixSeparatorIssue` and its assert. The Git ref rules that `getBranchPrefixIssue` applied inline move into `violatesRefFormat`, which both checks share. The separator is checked where it lands, as `a<sep>a`, so `-`, `_` and `.` pass while `..`, `//` and `/.` fail. `//` was added to the shared rules. It cannot change prefix results, because prefix normalization already collapses slash runs.
14	- `src/main/ipc/worktree-branch-name.ts` adds `getConfiguredBranchHead`, the prefix plus separator that every prefixed branch starts with. `computeBranchName` joins with it. `computeValidatedBranchName` validates the separator after the prefix. A git-username prefix that fails validation still skips prefixing entirely, so the separator only matters when a prefix is applied.
15	- `src/main/agent-hooks/first-work-branch-rename.ts` found branch leaves by slicing after the last `/` in two places. With a dash separator both kept the prefix. First, the eligibility check saw `jd-Nautilus` rather than the creature name `Nautilus`, so auto-rename from first work never fired. Second, the renamed branch's display name became "Jd fix auth" and its folder `jd-fix-auth`. The check now accepts either the slash leaf or the name after the configured head. The slash leaf keeps branches created before a separator change eligible. The renamed leaf is the branch minus the head. Settings and the git username are now read before the eligibility check, where they used to be read after generation. `stripConfiguredBranchPrefix` needed no change. It strips the prefix from the model's kebab-case slug, where every separator already reads as `-`.
16	- `GlobalSettings` gains `branchPrefixSeparator` with default `/`. The runtime settings contracts that carry `branchPrefixCustom` carry it too.
17	- `GitPane.tsx` moves the existing draft-and-echo logic of the prefix input into a `useSettingDraft` hook, and the new separator input reuses it.
18	
19	Known gaps, left for follow-ups:
20	
21	- The draft title for a new pull request comes from the branch leaf after the last `/` (`create-review-draft-title.ts`). With a dash separator it keeps the prefix ("Jd feat login form"). The field is editable. Fixing it needs the configured head in the renderer, including the git username.
22	- The separator is checked on its own, between two plain characters. Some contrived prefix and separator pairs pass both checks and Git still rejects the joined name, for example prefix `foo.lo` with separator `k/`. Git stays authoritative at creation, and the error names the branch.
23	- There is no way to choose an empty separator. A blank field means `/`.
24	
25	Out of scope: per-project prefixes (#18103) and the folder template (#5082). A branch token in that template would pick the separator up through `computeBranchName`.
26	
27	## Verification
28	
29	- `src/shared/branch-prefix.test.ts` and `src/shared/branch-name-from-work.test.ts` pass (67 tests). They include new cases for accepted separators (`/ - _ . --`, empty, missing) and rejected ones (`.. // /. .lock/ @{ ~ : space \`).
30	- The new `computeBranchName` and `computeValidatedBranchName` cases in `src/main/ipc/worktree-logic.test.ts` pass: dash join, blank-separator fallback, no-prefix, `jd/` + `-` giving `jd-feature`, and rejection of `..`. 31	- `src/main/agent-hooks/first-work-branch-rename.test.ts` passes (41 tests). Running it here needed a throwaway vitest config outside the repo that resolves packages from the pnpm store. It has a new case: current branch `jd-Nautilus`, head `jd-`. The branch is renamed to `jd-fix-auth`, the display name is "Fix auth" and the folder leaf is `fix-auth`. With the head-stripped leaf removed from the eligibility check, that case fails, so the test guards the fix. The module mock gains `getConfiguredBranchHead`, which defaults to the same `you/` behaviour as the existing mocks.
32	- The checkout has unbuilt workspace packages and missing React types, so `tsc` cannot load the project configs. A standalone strict typecheck of the changed files reports no errors in the changed `.ts` sources. `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on every changed file.
33	- The settings UI was not exercised in a running app.
34	
35	## Topology
36	
37	`abbd diff`: no topology change. No units, contracts or relations between modules came or went. The change stays inside existing modules and their current couplings. `.abbd/` was re-synced and is committed with the code.

## Why

Teams whose branch convention uses a dash (`jd-feat-login-form`) could not use the branch prefix setting, because Orca always joined prefix and name with `/`. They had to edit the branch field on every new workspace or pass `--branch` from the CLI. This adds a separator setting so the prefix setting works for them, and leaves everyone else on `/`.

## What changes for users

Settings > Git > Branch Prefix gets a small separator input next to the prefix field, defaulting to `/`. With prefix `jd` and separator `-`, a workspace named `feat: login form` gets the branch `jd-feat-login-form`. The feedback line under the inputs previews the real join (`jd-feature`) and flags a separator git would reject.

A blank separator falls back to `/`. Existing settings files have no value and load the default, so nothing changes for current setups.

## How

- `GlobalSettings.branchPrefixSeparator` (default `/`) is a new field. It is optional on `BranchPrefixSettings` and on the runtime store contract, so a runtime that receives settings from an older client keeps the slash.
- `computeBranchName` joins with `normalizeBranchPrefixSeparator(settings.branchPrefixSeparator)`. `computeValidatedBranchName` now delegates the join to it, so the join lives in one place.
- `getBranchPrefixSeparatorIssue` runs the separator through `getBranchPrefixIssue` between two plain segments (`a<sep>b`). Separators with spaces, `~ ^ : ? * [ \`, `..`, `@{`, or a dot-leading path segment are rejected. Slash runs (`//`) are also rejected, because prefix normalization would otherwise hide them. Worktree creation throws a settings-pointing error for an invalid separator. Unlike an unusable git username, the separator is always user-configured, so it is never silently skipped.
- The first-work auto-rename hook used to find the branch leaf by slicing after the last `/`. With a dash separator, `jd-crab` would never be recognized as an auto-generated creature name, and auto-rename would silently stop. `getBranchLeaf` strips the configured `prefix + separator` when it matches and otherwise falls back to the last `/` segment, so branches created under older settings still work. The hook resolves the git username before the creature check to make this possible, and only under the git-username strategy, matching the creation path.
- `stripConfiguredBranchPrefix` needed no change. It compares dash-slugified text, so a model echoing `jd/` or `jd-` is stripped either way.
- The prefix input's draft-and-echo handling moved into a small `useSettingTextDraft` hook, which the separator input reuses.

## Known limitation

With a non-slash separator, auto-rename can only find the creature leaf when the current prefix resolves to what the branch was created with. A branch like `jdoe-crab` is skipped for good in two cases. One is a git username lookup that comes back empty at rename time. The other is a change to the prefix or separator after the branch exists. The slash separator is unaffected because the last-`/` fallback still applies. Treating an unresolved prefix as retry rather than settled would close the first case. That changes the hook's retry policy, so it is left for a follow-up.

## Not in scope

The per-project prefix (#18103) and the folder template branch token (#5082) are not implemented here. Both would read the same separator through `computeBranchName`.

Both PRs make the same core changes in the same places: `BranchPrefixSettings` and the new normalizer go in `src/shared/branch-prefix.ts`, `GlobalSettings` gets the field with a `/` default, the runtime contracts get an optional `branchPrefixSeparator`, the join changes in `computeBranchName` and `computeValidatedBranchName`, the rename hook in `first-work-branch-rename.ts` is fixed, and `GitPane` pulls its draft-and-echo logic into a hook. The comment in `config/scripts/verify-localization-catalog.mjs` says "Feature PRs own English declarations". The check also flags code references missing from the catalog (around line 590), so X probably fails CI. Y adds the keys to `en.json` and the other 10 locales, and also makes the setting findable by searching "separator".
- **Reuse.** Y checks the separator with the existing `getBranchPrefixIssue(\`a${sep}b\`)`, which is what the issue asked for. `computeValidatedBranchName` then calls `computeBranchName`, so the join happens in one place. - **Where X is better.** X's `assertBranchPrefixSeparatorValid` matches the existing `assertBranchPrefixValid`; Y writes the throw inline. X's `getConfiguredBranchHead` sits next to `getConfiguredBranchPrefix`; Y's `getBranchLeaf` is fine in the shared module. X's hook takes the commit callback, which is a little tidier.
- **Y's flaws.** In the de, ja, ko, tr, zh and zh-Hant catalogs, the separator error message is missing the `\` character. The keys are readable names rather than the hashed style around them, though readable keys like `jiraIssueKeyCasingTitle` already exist.

- **Y** is shorter. Its verification is stronger in one way: it compares failure counts with the base commit. But it never mentions the draft-title gap. Its stated limitation is real, but it's about a less common edge case.
